source.title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: A valued field (K, v) is called a tame field if its algebraic closure K^ac, equipped with the unique extension of v, is a tame extension of (K, v). An algebraic extension (L|K, v) of a henselian valued field is called tame if every finite subextension K'|K satisfies: (T1) the ramification index (vK' : vK) is not divisible by char Kv, (T2) the residue field extension K'v|Kv is separable, and (T3) the extension (K'|K, v) is defectless (i.e., [K':K] = (vK':vK)[K'v:Kv]). It is known that tame fields (K, v) satisfy model completeness in the language L_val of valued rings relative to the elementary theories of their value groups vK (in the language of ordered groups) and their residue fields Kv (in the language of rings). Do tame fields admit quantifier elimination in a suitable (possibly enriched) language?
accepted.context_brief: Quantifier elimination for tame valued fields

evidence.quote: Open problem 1: Do tame fields admit quantifier elimination in a suitable language? The problem is that we do not know enough about purely wild extensions, i.e., algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field that are linearly disjoint from tame extensions.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime. Consider the fields Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}), where Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) is the totally ramified extension of the p-adic field Q_p obtained by adjoining all p^n-th roots of unity (n in N), and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) is the totally ramified extension obtained by adjoining a compatible system of p^n-th roots of p (n in N). Both fields, equipped with their unique extensions of the p-adic valuation v_p, are not Kaplansky fields (i.e., they do not satisfy Kaplansky's hypothesis (A) from 1942), and therefore admit uncountably many maximal immediate extensions with distinct elementary L_val-theories, of which uncountably many are not decidable. The maximal immediate extensions that do have decidable elementary L_val-theories (as shown by Kartas 2024) are tame fields. What is the internal valuation-theoretic or algebraic structure of these maximal immediate extensions (beyond the fact that there are infinitely many of them)? What structural properties of such an extension distinguish the decidable ones from the undecidable ones?
accepted.context_brief: Structure of maximal immediate extensions of Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty})

evidence.quote: Open problem 2: What is the structure of these extensions (apart from the fact that they are infinite)? What are the indications in their structure that distinguish the decidable from the undecidable extensions?

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime. Consider the following valued fields with their canonical p-adic (or t-adic) valuations: (a) Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}), the totally ramified extension of Q_p obtained by adjoining all p^n-th roots of unity; (b) Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}), the totally ramified extension of Q_p obtained by adjoining a compatible system of p^n-th roots of p; (c) Q_p^{ab}, the maximal abelian extension of Q_p; (d) F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}, the perfect hull of the Laurent series field F_p((t)) over the field F_p with p elements, with its t-adic valuation; (e) F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty}, the perfect hull of the Laurent series field over the algebraic closure F_p^{ac} of F_p. Here L_val denotes the language of valued rings, and L_val(t) denotes L_val enriched with a constant symbol for the element t. Are the fields Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}), Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}), and Q_p^{ab} decidable in the language L_val? Are F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} and F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} decidable in L_val, or even in L_val(t)?
accepted.context_brief: Decidability of Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}), Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}), Q_p^{ab}, and their positive-characteristic analogues

evidence.quote: Open problem 3: Are Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}), Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) and Q_p^{ab} decidable in L_val ? Are F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} and F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} decidable in L_val or even L_val(t)? Here F_p^{ac} denotes the algebraic closure of F_p.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime. The perfectoid transfer theorem of Kartas (2024) provides implications from decidability in positive characteristic to decidability in mixed characteristic: (a) if F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} (the perfect hull of F_p((t)), with t-adic valuation) has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) have decidable elementary or existential L_val-theories respectively; (b) if F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val(t)-theory, then Q_p^{ab} has a decidable elementary or existential L_val-theory. (Here L_val is the language of valued rings and L_val(t) adds a constant for t.) It is also known (from the tilt correspondence) that decidability in L_val transfers from perfectoid fields to their tilts, giving partial converses. The precise open question is: can the argument be improved to obtain decidability in L_val(t) on the positive characteristic side, given decidability in L_val on the mixed characteristic side? That is, if Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory (not merely L_val)? And if Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty} have a decidable L_val(t)-theory?
accepted.context_brief: Reverse direction of the perfectoid transfer theorem for decidability

evidence.quote: Open problem 4: What about the reverse direction? In fact, if Q_p(zeta_{p^infty}) or Q_p(p^{1/p^infty}) has a decidable L_val-theory, then F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} has a decidable L_val-theory, and if Q_p^{ab} has a decidable L_val-theory, then so does F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^infty}. ... So a more precise version of problem 4 is whether this argument can be improved to get decidability in L_val(t) on the positive characteristic side.

accepted.question_text: A nontrivially valued field (K, v) is called deeply ramified if it satisfies two conditions: (DRvg) no archimedean component of the value group vK is discrete (i.e., for any two convex subgroups Gamma_1 strictly contained in Gamma_2 of vK, the quotient Gamma_2/Gamma_1 is not isomorphic to Z); and (DRvr) if the residue characteristic char Kv = p > 0, then O_K/pO_K is semiperfect (Frobenius surjective) when char K = 0, and the completion's valuation ring O_{K-hat}/pO_{K-hat} is semiperfect when char K = p. The class of deeply ramified fields contains all perfectoid fields (complete nondiscrete rank-1 valued fields of residue characteristic p with semiperfect O_K/pO_K) and all tame fields. A roughly deeply ramified (rdr) field satisfies (DRvr) together with (DRvp): if char Kv = p > 0, then v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK. Model-theoretic results analogous to those for tame fields (model completeness relative to value group and residue field) have been established for roughly tame fields (henselian fields satisfying (TF2) Kv perfect, (TF3) algebraically maximal, and the weaker (TF1r): if char Kv = p > 0 the interval [-v(p), v(p)] in vK is p-divisible). What can be said about the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields relative to their value groups and residue fields, and in particular what are the model-theoretic properties of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty} (the perfect hull of the formal Laurent series field F_p((t))), which is a deeply ramified field of positive characteristic?
accepted.context_brief: Model theory of deeply/roughly deeply ramified fields, especially F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}

evidence.quote: Open problem 5: What can we say about the model theory of (roughly) deeply ramified fields (relative to their value groups and residue fields), and in particular of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}?

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime and let F_p be the field with p elements. Let F_p(t) be the rational function field in one variable t over F_p, with the t-adic valuation v_t (which sends a rational function to the order of vanishing at t = 0). Let (F_p(t)^h, v_t) denote the henselization of (F_p(t), v_t), and let (F_p((t)), v_t) denote the formal Laurent series field over F_p with its t-adic valuation. It is known that (F_p(t)^h, v_t) is existentially closed in (F_p((t)), v_t) in the language L_val of valued rings. Is (F_p(t)^h, v_t) an elementary substructure of (F_p((t)), v_t) in L_val (i.e., do they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences in L_val)?
accepted.context_brief: Elementary equivalence: henselization of F_p(t) vs. F_p((t))

evidence.quote: Open problem 6: Is F_p(t)^h an elementary substructure of F_p((t))? In contrast, Jahnke and Kartas prove that F_p(t^{1/p^infty})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}.

accepted.question_text: A henselian valued field (K, v) is called a tame field if: (TF1) when char Kv = p > 0, the value group vK is p-divisible; (TF2) the residue field Kv is perfect; and (TF3) (K, v) is algebraically maximal (admits no nontrivial immediate algebraic extensions). Tame fields satisfy model completeness and relative decidability (in the equicharacteristic positive case) in the language L_val of valued rings relative to their value groups and residue fields. A henselian valued field is called a perfect valued field of positive characteristic if it has positive characteristic and its residue field is perfect. Is it possible to prove model-theoretic results for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic analogous to those for tame fields, perhaps under mild additional conditions?
accepted.context_brief: Model theory for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic

evidence.quote: Open problem 7: Is it possible to prove model theoretic results for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic, analoguous to those for tame fields (but under mild additional conditions)?

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime and F_p the field with p elements. Let F_p((t)) denote the field of formal Laurent series over F_p, equipped with the t-adic valuation v_t (which assigns to each nonzero series the smallest exponent with nonzero coefficient). The decidability of the elementary theory of Q_p (the p-adic numbers) in the language L_val of valued rings has been known since 1965 (Ax-Kochen, Ershov). It is known that the L_val(t)-elementary axiom system (A_t) consisting of 'henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a Z-group with smallest positive element v(t) and residue field F_p' is not complete (Kuhlmann 2001). What can be said about the model theory of F_p((t)) in L_val? In particular, is there a complete axiomatization of the L_val-elementary theory of F_p((t)), and is this theory decidable?
accepted.context_brief: Complete axiomatization and decidability of F_p((t))

evidence.quote: Open problem 8: What can we say about the model theory and in particular a complete axiomatization and the decidability of F_p((t))?

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime and F_p the field with p elements. Let (F_p((t)), v_t) be the field of formal Laurent series over F_p with the t-adic valuation. It is shown (Kuhlmann 2001) that there exist henselian defectless valued fields that are not existentially closed in their maximal immediate extensions in the language L_val of valued rings. Specifically, there exists an extension (L, v) of (F_p((t)), v_t) that is a henselian defectless field satisfying the same axiom system, yet (L, v) is not L_val-existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions. A valued field (K, v) is existentially closed in an extension if every existential L_val-sentence true in the extension is already true in (K, v). Is there a natural or 'handy' additional condition on the immediate algebraic extensions of a henselian defectless valued field (K, v) that guarantees (K, v) is existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions?
accepted.context_brief: Conditions for existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions

evidence.quote: Open problem 9: Is there a handy additional condition on the immediate extensions that remedies this situation?

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime and F_p the field with p elements. An extremal valued field is a valued field (K, v) such that for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1, ..., X_n) over K, the set {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_1,...,a_n in O_K} (where O_K is the valuation ring) has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}. This is an L_val-elementary axiom scheme. The L_val-elementary axiom system (A) is: 'henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a Z-group and residue field F_p.' It is known (Kuhlmann 2001) that (A) alone is not complete. It is also known (Azgin-Kuhlmann-Pop 2012) that F_p((t)) is an extremal field. Is the axiom system (A) together with the extremality axiom scheme — that is, the theory of henselian defectless valued fields of positive characteristic with Z-group value group, residue field F_p, and extremality — a complete axiom system for the L_val-theory of F_p((t))?
accepted.context_brief: Completeness of (A) + extremality as axiom system for F_p((t))

evidence.quote: Open problem 10: Is (A) + "(K, v) is extremal" a complete axiom system?

accepted.question_text: A valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1,...,X_n) over K, the set of values {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_i in O_K} has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}, where O_K is the valuation ring. A valuation v on K is said to be a composition v = w ∘ w-bar if there are valuations w and w-bar such that w is a coarsening of v (i.e., every v-open set is w-open) and w-bar is the valuation induced by v on the residue field Kw of w, so that (K, v) maps into (K, w) with residue (Kw, w-bar). It is known that if v = w ∘ w-bar and w has divisible value group, then both w and w-bar can be studied using the structure of v. Is it true that: if both w and w-bar are extremal and w has divisible value group, then v = w ∘ w-bar is also extremal?
accepted.context_brief: Extremality under composition: does extremality of components with divisible coarse part imply extremality of the composition?

evidence.quote: Open problem 11: If v = w ∘ w-bar with w and w-bar extremal and w has divisible value group, does it follow that v is extremal?

accepted.question_text: A valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1,...,X_n) over K, the set {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_i in O_K} has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}. A valuation v can be written as a composition v = w ∘ w-bar, meaning w is a coarsening of v and w-bar is the valuation induced by v on the residue field Kw of w. It is known that if v = w ∘ w-bar is extremal, then the finer component w-bar is also extremal. Does it follow that the coarser component w is also extremal?
accepted.context_brief: Extremality of the coarse component in a composition of valuations

evidence.quote: Open problem 12: We know that if v = w ∘ w-bar is extremal, then so is w-bar (see [6, Lemma 4.1]). But does it also follow that w is extremal?

accepted.question_text: A valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every multivariate polynomial f(X_1,...,X_n) over K, the set {v(f(a_1,...,a_n)) | a_i in O_K} has a maximal element in vK union {infinity}, where O_K is the valuation ring. A valued field (M, v) is called a maximal immediate extension of (K, v) if (M|K, v) is an immediate extension (same value group and same residue field) and (M, v) admits no further nontrivial immediate extensions. It is known that every extremal valued field is henselian and defectless, and that there exist henselian defectless fields (e.g., certain extensions of F_p((t))) that are not existentially closed in their maximal immediate extensions. Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions (i.e., does every existential L_val-sentence true in a maximal immediate extension of an extremal field already hold in the extremal field itself)?
accepted.context_brief: Extremal fields and existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions

evidence.quote: Open problem 13: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field. A field K is called large if it is existentially closed in the power series field K((t)) in the language of rings. Hypothesis (R4) states: for an arbitrary field K, if a function field F|K (a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree at least 1) admits a K-rational place (a valuation on F with residue field isomorphic to K), then K is existentially closed in F. It is known that local uniformization of rational places of arbitrary function fields (in all characteristics and all dimensions) implies (R4). By the work of Hironaka, local uniformization holds in characteristic 0. It is also known (Anscombe-Dittmann-Fehm 2023) that if (R4) holds, then the existential L_val(t)-theory of F_p((t)) (the formal Laurent series field over F_p in variable t, with t-adic valuation) is decidable. Does hypothesis (R4) hold in general (i.e., for all fields K and all function fields F|K with a K-rational place, is K existentially closed in F)?
accepted.context_brief: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? (Large fields existentially closed in function fields with rational place)

accepted.question_text: Local uniformization is a local version of resolution of singularities: given a valuation v on the function field F of an algebraic variety, local uniformization asks for a model of F in which the center of v is regular (a non-singular point). It is known (de Jong 1996) that resolution by alteration holds: one can resolve singularities after passing to a finite extension of the function field. Knaf and Kuhlmann (2009) proved local uniformization by alteration for arbitrary valuations: every place on a function field admits local uniformization in a finite extension of that function field. Hypothesis (R4) states that any large field K is existentially closed in any function field F|K that admits a K-rational place. (1) Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable and useful weakening '(R4) by alteration' (perhaps: given a large field K and a function field F|K with a K-rational place, there is a finite extension K'|K such that K' is existentially closed in F.K')? (2) Is there a coherent 'model theory by alteration', i.e., a systematic framework in which model-theoretic properties of valued fields can be established after passing to a finite field extension?
accepted.context_brief: Model theory by alteration: (R4)-analogue and model theory after finite extensions

evidence.quote: Open problem 15: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable (and useful) hypothesis "(R4) by alteration"? Is there a "model theory by alteration"?

accepted.question_text: Let (K, v) be a henselian valued field. A finite Galois extension E = (L|K, v) of prime degree p (where p = char Kv) with nontrivial defect (i.e., [L:K] > (vL:vK)[Lv:Kv]) is said to have independent defect if the set Sigma_E = {v(sigma(f)/f - 1) | f in L^x} (for any non-identity sigma in Gal(L|K)) satisfies: Sigma_E = {alpha in vK | alpha > H_E} for some proper convex subgroup H_E of vK such that vK/H_E has no smallest positive element. Otherwise E has dependent defect. The field (K, v) is called an independent defect field if, for some extension of v to K' = K(zeta_p) (a primitive p-th root of unity, or K' = K in characteristic p), all Galois extensions of (K', v) of prime degree p with nontrivial defect have independent defect. A valued field (K, v) is called roughly deeply ramified (rdr) if it satisfies: (DRvp) if char Kv = p > 0, then v(p) is not the smallest positive element of vK; and (DRvr) if char Kv = p > 0, then the completion's O_{K-hat}/pO_{K-hat} is semiperfect. It is proven (Kuhlmann-Rzepka 2023) that every algebraic extension of a roughly deeply ramified field is an independent defect field, and (Rzepka-Szewczyk 2023) that a henselian field is roughly tame (satisfying (TF1r): if char Kv = p > 0 then [-v(p),v(p)] is p-divisible; (TF2): Kv is perfect; (TF3): algebraically maximal) if and only if all its algebraic extensions are defectless fields. By analogy, the conjecture is that a henselian field is roughly deeply ramified if and only if all its algebraic extensions are independent defect fields. Is this conjecture true? That is, if all algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field (K, v) are independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified field?
accepted.context_brief: Converse of Kuhlmann-Rzepka: characterization of rdr fields via independent defect property

evidence.quote: Open problem 16: If all algebraic extensions of a henselian field (K, v) are independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified field?
